adpilot.note: adpilot's own ad copy; a kept failure (AD-006, two variants) is in the population

listing.why: the path calls bojo_tools.publishing.compose_listing -> reasoning_tasks.listing_proposal; ty/services.json gives listingforge the compose_listing tool and calls it ListingForge copy

ppc.why: upload -> proposal -> approve -> write -> download are the /api/design-studio/amazon-files/* endpoints in design_studio_api.py, and the surface is Design Studio -> Ads -> Amazon files (northstar-os-ui/src/pages/internal/design-studio/AmazonFiles.jsx). AdPilot only reads the imported bulksheets, so it is not the producer of this artefact.
ppc.never_blended: design-studio's published seller score comes from the image pass. These rows are a separate population and are reported, never averaged with it.

golden_goose.why: the path calls bojo_tools.sourcing.golden_goose_scan, which is the golden_goose_scan tool. ty/services.json now carries ONE Golden Goose: 'golden-goose' at /golden-goose. The legacy 'goldengoose' id is an alias of it (the route redirects), so the sample is owned by the real service and the alias adds no second sample.
golden_goose.alias_note: the alias is declared here, not inferred: it adds no brief and no sample, it resolves the retired id to the one service that produces the artefact.

scan.why: bojo_tools.sourcing_extra.scan_products is Product Finder's declared tool (ty/services.json tools: [scan_products]). The scanner is injected with a recorded candidate cache because a live search is a gated, paid action; the term filter, the caller's limit, the cache provenance and the refusal-by-name are the app's own code, and the scan computes no economics - the check that it added no field says so.
scan.recorded_answer: the candidate cache is a fixture: a live search is a gated, paid action. Nothing in this path contacts Amazon.

research.why: no service in ty/services.json declares a path that reaches research_graph.research: the module is exercised by its own test only, and nothing in the registry or the backend calls it. The pass is measured and reported, but attributing it to product-finder (or anything else) would be inventing an owner.

offer_copy.why: the room asks the local engine for TITLE:/BULLETS:/KEYWORDS: and shows the answer; the copy is judged by specialists.listing_optimizer (audit_title, audit_bullet, keyword_coverage, backend_bytes), which is the app's own listing rubric, plus the claims lint. ty/services.json gives offerchisel exactly that product: a title, four bullets and back-end search terms.
offer_copy.recorded_answer: the engine answer is a recorded fixture: a live generation is a gated model call. Every rule applied to it is the app's own deterministic code.

caption.why: the room writes ONE caption plus 3-4 hashtags for a brief and a platform (TownCrier.jsx:19 prompt, :22-30 parser). ty/services.json gives towncrier that purpose and the room declares write_content, the caption writer with the claim screen. The checks are the room's own limits (220 chars), its brand rule ('Word Coffee is NOT a beverage'), the claims lint and the hashtag shape.
caption.recorded_answer: the engine answer is a recorded fixture: a live generation is a gated model call. Every rule applied to it is the app's own or the room's own, stated in the brief.

social_caption.why: this path is the app's own code end to end: social_pulse.generate_caption is called with the local model refused, so the documented template fallback runs. The caption, hashtags, CTA, platform spec and the app's own _score_caption are SocialPulse's output, not a fixture.
social_caption.never_blended: the caption checks describe the deterministic fallback path; a live model answer is a gated, paid action and is not measured here.

research.why_unattributed: no service in ty/services.json declares a path that reaches research_graph.research: the module is exercised by its own test only, and nothing in the registry or the backend calls it. The pass is measured and reported, but attributing it to product-finder (or anything else) would be inventing an owner.

pipeline.why_it_matters: sel-06 (2026-11-11): the pass renders through the same product_picture.build the API calls, so the number describes the product. The plate is named above: when it is 'drawn' the picture's photograph is a stand-in and only the artwork, warp and gate are real.

ceiling.note: the published mean is over generated/composite outputs. Only 12 of 56 briefs have a reference on disk that can be cut out and verified; the other 44 cannot be produced honestly here (32 prompt-only, 12 with no local reference copy). Counting those as zero would be a pipeline verdict on evidence that does not exist; counting them as passes would be invention.
